Name: Daya
Build: Wiry, narrow shoulders, long forearms; Act 1 fed and fit; changes by act (see states)
Skin: Medium wheatish Punjabi; sun-weathered forearms and neck; pallor rises with disease
Hair: Black, cropped short (cut hair, no turban), faint early grey at the temples; Act 2 matted and overgrown; Act 5-6 thinning
Beard: Act 1 trimmed stubble; Act 2 three-week unkempt beard; Act 3 clean-shaven; Act 4 short full beard (legend); Act 5-6 sparse and patchy
OutfitSummer: Half-sleeve checked shirt over a white vest; dark jeans; leather sandals
OutfitMonsoon: Quick-dry polyester shirt; dark trousers; rubber chappals
OutfitWinter: Cheap black faux-leather jacket over a sweatshirt; jeans; canvas sports shoes; wool muffler
OutfitByAct: A1=above (collection-run gangster: gold-plated chain removed); A2=faded kurta and loose pyjama in rags or one donated blanket and a plastic sheet in rain; A3=plain cotton shirt and trousers then tracksuit; A4=muted shalwar kameez and waistcoat (Karachi) with a topi only for Friday prayers in the legend; A5=the same kurta hanging loose and sweat-stained; A6=oversized hooded sweatshirt and cardigan that no longer fit
Accessories: Steel kada on the right wrist; a steel katora (begging bowl) and cloth bag in Act 2; cheap digital watch; no phone from Act 2
GaitNotes: Act 1: loose confident stride, slight forward lean, hands in pockets. Act 2: shortened stride, rounded shoulders, avoids eye contact, rests on one hip while standing. Act 4: deliberate neutral Karachi walk that he consciously holds. Act 5-6: hunched 9 degrees, slow, hand pressed to ribs, rests after stairs; a cough fit bends him double (input lock 2-4 s).
Tells: Cracks his LEFT thumb when he lies (UCastTellComponent 'ThumbCrack'); counts everything under his breath (rupees, steps, chapatis); says little
Voice: Low, dry, economical; Lahori Punjabi with a Kasur accent, functional Urdu; breath gets shorter as the disease progresses
SensitivityNote: Born in Mamdot; grandparents from Kasur. Faith practice is kept low-key and respectful: kada, no caricature; the disease is shown as a body, not a spectacle.

Name: Sukhi
Build: Medium, strong forearms from kneading and lifting tiffin carriers
Skin: Medium wheatish; flushed cheeks from the kitchen heat; faint flour dust on forearms in Act 1-2
Hair: Long black hair in one oiled braid; a few early silver strands; chunni drawn over head at the gurdwara
OutfitSummer: Light cotton salwar kameez in muted colours; thin dupatta
OutfitMonsoon: Cotton salwar kameez; dupatta pinned; plastic slippers
OutfitWinter: Salwar kameez with a hand-knitted cardigan and a shawl
OutfitByAct: A1=printed everyday salwar kameez with an apron over it at work; A2=the same suits, mended and worn; A5=the last day: a plain suit she would wear to the gurdwara
Accessories: Thin gold earrings; steel or gold kada; bangles; steel tiffin carriers and a cloth bundle; no heavy makeup
GaitNotes: Quick, practical walk carrying weight on the hip or head; stops to check the boy; stands with arms folded when worried
Tells: Taps the rim of a steel tiffin lid when she is angry and not saying it
Voice: Warm, direct, quick Punjabi; unsentimental; lowers her voice rather than raises it
SensitivityNote: A working mother and small-business owner, shown with competence. Her death in Act 5 is never used as spectacle.

Name: Gurnoor
Skin: Medium wheatish, a shade lighter than his father; sunburnt nose
Hair: Black, uncut, kept in a top-knot (joora) under a small patka outdoors
OutfitSummer: Cotton T-shirt and shorts; rubber chappals; patka in a school or festival colour
OutfitMonsoon: Plastic raincoat or a school jacket; shorts; sandals
OutfitWinter: Hand-knit sweater and a woollen cap over the patka; track pants; canvas shoes
OutfitByAct: A1 and A2=the same cricket-and-school wardrobe, a size bigger in Act 2 (hand-me-downs); A5=school uniform
Accessories: Plastic cricket bat and a rubber ball; school bag; a thin steel kada
GaitNotes: Runs everywhere; bat swung over the shoulder; scuffs his feet; shy stop-and-stare when his father comes home
Tells: Counts runs out loud like his father counts rupees
Voice: Child Punjabi with a Ghaziabad Hindi edge; excitable, asks questions
SensitivityNote: A child; never shown in a threatening or exploitative frame; the Act 5 scene is staged off screen.

Name: Bibi
Skin: Fair-wheatish, deeply lined; age spots on the hands; slightly cloudy left eye
Hair: White, braided and pinned beneath the chunni
OutfitSummer: White cotton salwar kameez; white chunni over the head
OutfitMonsoon: White cotton suit; plastic sandals; a cotton shawl
OutfitWinter: White suit; thick woollen shawl; woollen socks; a hand-knit cardigan
OutfitByAct: Same wardrobe in every act; she wears white because she is a widow and she does not change it
Accessories: Wooden walking stick; thick-framed glasses on a cord; a small prayer book in a cloth; a steel kada; a transistor radio
GaitNotes: Short shuffling steps, one hand on the stick and the other on a wall or shoulder; sits down in stages; stands up with a grunt and a joke
Tells: Calls the boy by his grandfather's name when tired; hums a Kasur lullaby
Voice: Cracked, patient old Lahori Punjabi; the source of Daya's accent; sings when she thinks nobody listens
SensitivityNote: Respected elder; head covering is correct and consistent; never played for pity.

Name: Bablu
Role: Daya's former partner; the man on the balcony
Build: Big, heavy-shouldered, soft belly over strong legs; 20 kg heavier than Daya's Act 1 weight
Skin: Fair wheatish, flushed; heavy jaw; shaving rash
Hair: Thick black hair gelled back; thin patch at the crown
Beard: Heavy moustache with a closely trimmed beard
OutfitSummer: Branded half-sleeve shirt, unbuttoned one too many; formal trousers; leather slip-ons
OutfitMonsoon: Dark shirt; cargo pants; rubber-soled shoes
OutfitWinter: Quilted puffer jacket with a fictional logo; wool cap
OutfitByAct: A1=flashy, new money; A6=the same style, older and a bit too tight; he lives above a shop in a fourth-floor flat
Accessories: Heavy gold chain; gold rings on three fingers; a smartphone; a fictional-brand watch; an SUV key fob (fictional)
GaitNotes: Wide stance; chest first; sits with his legs apart; breathes through his mouth after one flight of stairs but wins a clinch because of mass
Tells: Never looks at the person he is lying to; touches the chain when he decides
Voice: Loud, jovial, Western UP Hindi, Haryanvi edges; threats are delivered softly
SensitivityNote: A criminal, written as a person: friendly, afraid, defensive. No stereotype of a region or caste.

Name: Mangal
Role: Beggar at Nizamuddin; Daya's teacher of the platform economy
Build: Powerful chest, shoulders and forearms; bilateral above-knee amputee (about 18 cm of residual thigh); lower legs absent
OutfitSummer: Faded clean cotton kurta; the cut ends of his pyjama folded and secured with neat cloth wraps; a gamchha
OutfitMonsoon: Plastic sheet over the shoulders; kurta; waterproof board cover
OutfitWinter: Donated wool sweater; thick blanket tucked around the board; wool cap
OutfitByAct: A2=the Nizamuddin platform; the Coda=the same clothes, a better board, and a Rs 500 note
Accessories: A low wooden board about 90 x 45 cm on four ball-bearing caster wheels; two wooden hand blocks (pushers) with rubber grips; a tin cup; a transistor; a laminated medical card
GaitNotes: Moves seated on the board; pushes with the hand blocks, glides, pivots on a single hand; cannot climb stairs or curbs over 6 cm without help; speed about 1.0-1.4 m/s; stops at the same spots every day; sits upright with dignity, not slumped
Tells: Counts the day's coins into his lap twice; always names the exact figure
Voice: Dry, funny, exact; a lifetime of Delhi Hindi/Urdu; says 'fifty more than yesterday' like a prayer
SensitivityNote: Depict with dignity: a working man with expertise, humour and agency. No pity framing, no leering camera. The board is maintained and personal. Lower-limb absence is a mesh/animation setup, not a visual gag.

Name: Khanna
Skin: Fair wheatish; fine lines; slight tan from the garden
OutfitSummer: White cotton shirt, light trousers; soft shoes
OutfitMonsoon: Same with a dark umbrella and a rain-darkened hem
OutfitWinter: Charcoal or grey bandhgala (Nehru) jacket over a kurta; grey shawl
OutfitByAct: A3=station scene in a plain kurta and shawl (no uniform, no flag); A5-6=hospital and farm scenes in a grey sweater; Coda=the same bandhgala
Accessories: Thin steel-framed glasses; an old wristwatch with a leather strap; a cloth handkerchief; a small notebook
GaitNotes: Unhurried, upright, hands behind his back or folded; a slight hip stiffness on stairs; never rushes
Tells: Remembers and repeats names; pauses before the second sentence; when tired a Lahori vowel slips (the seven years)
Voice: Soft, never raised; unhurried; precise Hindi and Urdu, formal English, Lahori Punjabi he does not use in public
SensitivityNote: Fictional figure in the NSA mould, not any real official; no resemblance to a real face.

Name: Ravi
Build: Ex-army frame gone soft around the middle; powerful forearms
Skin: Wheatish; red cheeks and eye whites from drink; deep crow's feet
Hair: Short army cut, salt and pepper
OutfitSummer: Linen shirt with sleeves rolled; khaki chinos; leather loafers (Dubai) or kurta and loose trousers (Karachi)
OutfitMonsoon: Dark shirt; cotton trousers; a light rain jacket
OutfitWinter: Tweed or corduroy jacket; wool scarf
OutfitByAct: A3-A4=Dubai: pressed shirts, always a collar; A5=Karachi: stained shalwar kameez and a knee brace under it; the last day: the same, plus the lanyard of a fake fishing licence
Accessories: Steel-and-neoprene knee brace on the RIGHT knee; a hip flask (fictional label); worn Casio-style watch; a battered notebook; reading glasses
GaitNotes: Right knee wrecked: weight on the left, right leg swung slightly out and locked; stiff and cautious on stairs and slopes; sits whenever he can; the limp is permanent and slows him to 75% of normal (pairs with the injury rules of the vitals component)
Tells: Taps two fingers on the brace when he does not want to say something; always checks exits
Voice: Gravel; dry Delhi Hindi; the only person who calls Daya by his real name; softer when sober
SensitivityNote: His drinking is a wound, not a joke; his death in Act 5 is the emotional climax and is not staged for shock.

Name: Qureshi
Role: ISI counter-intelligence, Karachi station; the antagonist
Build: Lean, athletic, upright; the build of a man who runs at dawn
Hair: Short, neat, dark with a side parting
Beard: Trimmed short beard and moustache, always groomed
OutfitSummer: Pressed light-cotton shalwar kameez in white or ecru, or an open-collar shirt and chinos; polished shoes
OutfitMonsoon: Dark shalwar kameez; a folded umbrella
OutfitWinter: Wool waistcoat over a kurta; grey shawl; leather shoes
OutfitByAct: Same wardrobe across Act 4: he does not dress like an officer; the uniform appears only once
Accessories: A slim metal watch; reading glasses; a plain fountain pen; a worn paperback; prayer beads in the pocket (he prays; this is private, never a prop)
GaitNotes: Calm, measured, hands clasped behind his back; stops mid-stride to listen; turns the whole body toward a speaker
Tells: Never raises his voice; waits eight seconds for an answer; stirs tea in complete circles
Voice: Polite, precise Urdu with a Lahori cadence; excellent English; patient to the point of unease
SensitivityNote: An intelligent professional, not a cartoon villain; his faith is shown with respect and is never the reason he is the antagonist; Karachi and Lahore are rendered as real places.

Name: Sattar
Role: Boss of the Sattar network, Gulbahar Lines, Karachi
Build: Heavy, round-shouldered, diabetic: swollen ankles, careful steps
Skin: Medium-brown, mottled; darkened shins; tired eyes
Hair: White hair under a prayer cap
Beard: Full white beard, trimmed at the moustache line (the Hajj title is real, not a costume)
OutfitSummer: White cotton shalwar kameez; white crocheted prayer cap (topi); sandals; trouser hems above the ankle
OutfitMonsoon: The same; a dark waistcoat; rubber sandals
OutfitWinter: Cream shalwar kameez; woollen waistcoat; shawl; wool cap over the topi
OutfitByAct: A4=the same wardrobe; Friday: a spotless white suit and an attar fragrance; Eid: new clothes
Accessories: Prayer beads (tasbih); a glucometer and an insulin pen in a leather pouch; a walking stick with a silver head; thick-rimmed glasses; a worn Quran in a velvet cover (never used as a prop)
GaitNotes: Slow, rolling waddle with the weight on the heels; breath short on stairs; sits down in stages; the stick leans forward; pauses to check blood sugar
Tells: Counts his tasbih beads when he decides; says 'Insha'Allah' in two different tones: one honest, one a refusal
Voice: Deep, slow, courteous; Karachi Urdu with Sindhi turns; speaks of his obligations before his orders
SensitivityNote: A devout man and a gang boss; faith is shown as sincere and distinct from the crime; attire follows correct practice; no religious site hosts combat.

Name: Shahzaib
Role: Sattar's nephew and enforcer; Daya's closest friend in Karachi
Hair: Short fade, gelled at the front
OutfitSummer: Black polo; slim jeans; white sneakers; or a crisp shalwar kameez on Friday
OutfitByAct: A4=the same through the act; the Rangers raid: a plain shalwar kameez
Accessories: Sunglasses on the head; a large fictional-brand watch; a phone in a hard case; a gold ring; a motorbike helmet
GaitNotes: Easy, bouncing athlete's walk; takes the space; quick to touch a shoulder; never still
Tells: Taps the steering lock or his phone when he waits; laughs with the whole body before something violent
Voice: Fast, warm, joking Karachi Urdu; switches to English for slang; calls Daya 'Lahori'
SensitivityNote: Written as a likeable, ambitious young man whose loyalty is real; no stereotype of Karachi's youth.
